label: Payments and financial messaging
summary: Settles how the payment schemes apply: for PCI DSS the entity role, payment channels, card data handling and the level and route the acquirer sets; for SWIFT CSCF the architecture type, framework version and the independent assessment.

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 and PCI SSC SAQ documents; card-brand merchant and service-provider levels; acquirers and brands decide who validates and how

fields.label: Entity role
fields.note: Merchants and service providers have different levels and different SAQs; a service provider can only use SAQ D for service providers.

fields.label: Payment channels

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 section 4 and requirements 1.2.4, 12.5.1, 12.5.2: account data flows, CDE and connected-to systems

fields.note: Every channel through which account data enters or leaves. The channels decide which questionnaire or assessment fits.

fields.label: Card data handling

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 section 4: entities that store, process or transmit account data

fields.note: Whether the organisation itself stores, processes or transmits card numbers. Not known yet is fine: a data search finds out, including logs and dumps.

fields.label: Card data environment
fields.note: Whether a cardholder data environment exists: the systems that store, process or transmit card data, and those connected to them. Not determined yet is fine; scoping settles it.

fields.label: Payment systems
fields.note: The payment applications and systems involved, picked from the asset inventory. Leave empty if the inventory does not hold them yet.

fields.label: Web payment method

source.ref: PCI DSS v4.0.1 and PCI SSC SAQ A and A-EP: how a website takes the card decides the questionnaire

fields.note: How the website takes the card. It decides between the shortest questionnaire and a full assessment, and brings in the v4.0.1 script controls.

fields.label: Level
fields.note: Set by each card brand and the acquirer, not by the organisation: enter the highest level any brand assigns. Not assigned yet is allowed; ask the acquirer for it in writing.

fields.label: Validation route
options: Report on Compliance by a QSA
Report on Compliance by an ISA
fields.note: A QSA or an internal security assessor writes a Report on Compliance; smaller merchants use a self-assessment questionnaire. Always confirm with the acquirer.

fields.label: SAQ type
fields.note: A: card-not-present, all outsourced. A-EP: e-commerce site controls the redirect. B: imprint or dial-out terminals. B-IP: standalone IP terminals. C-VT: keying into a third-party virtual terminal. C: payment application online. P2PE: listed P2PE only. SPoC: phone with card reader. D: everyone else.

fields.label: Existing report
fields.note: A previous Report on Compliance or self-assessment questionnaire, with its Attestation of Compliance. It shows how the acquirer has had the organisation validate so far.

fields.label: Report file
fields.note: Optional: attach the report with its Attestation of Compliance. It is kept in Evidence.

source.ref: SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework: architecture types A1, A2, A3, A4 and B decide the applicable controls (swift.com was unreachable; read in consultancy guides)

fields.label: SWIFT user
fields.note: Whether the organisation connects to SWIFT itself or through a service bureau.

fields.label: Architecture type
fields.note: A1: you own the communication and messaging interfaces. A2: you own the messaging interface only. A3: a SWIFT-supplied connector for app-to-app. A4: your own connector. B: no local SWIFT infrastructure. A wrong type means the wrong controls.

fields.label: SWIFT systems
fields.note: The systems that support the SWIFT connection, picked from the asset inventory. Leave empty if the inventory does not hold them yet.

fields.label: CSCF version
fields.note: The version of the Customer Security Controls Framework the yearly attestation is made against.

fields.label: Attestation type

source.ref: SWIFT KYC-SA annual attestation by 31 December; independent assessment, internal or external (consultancy guides; swift.com unreachable)

fields.note: Whether this is the first attestation or a yearly one. Users attest to SWIFT each year.

fields.label: Assessor type

source.ref: SWIFT KYC-SA annual attestation by 31 December; independent assessment, internal or external (consultancy guides; swift.com unreachable)

fields.note: Who carries out the independent assessment. The assessor must be independent of the people who run the controls.

fields.label: Existing assessment

source.ref: SWIFT KYC-SA annual attestation by 31 December; independent assessment, internal or external (consultancy guides; swift.com unreachable)

fields.note: Prior findings can sometimes be reused if the last independent assessment ended under two years ago and nothing relevant changed (reported by consultancies; confirm with SWIFT).

fields.label: Assessment file
fields.note: Optional: attach the independent assessment report. It is kept in Evidence.

gate.label: A level has been assigned
gate.hint: Choose the level the acquirer gave, or ask the acquirer for it.

gate.label: The validation route is known
gate.hint: ROC or SAQ, as the acquirer states.
